theme: App download and ranking histories: App Store / Google Play rank scrapers, app-store-scraper, google-play-scraper, AppFigures/Sensor Tower/data.ai open samples, app review-count time series
queries_run: gh search repos "app store rank history scraper" --sort stars
gh search repos "app store review dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "app rank history" OR "app store ranking history" --sort updated

candidates.name: app-store-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js library (MIT, 1422 stars, updated 12 Sep 2026) that hits Apple's public iTunes/App Store lookup and search endpoints with no auth/API key. Returns per-app fields including current category rank, rating count (proxy for cumulative review count), rating average, price, and version history for any app id -- e.g. Airbnb's iOS app id 401626263, plus Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia. No data committed; a scheduled run would need to be built to accumulate a rank/review-count time series.
candidates.why_useful: Fills gap #5 (engagement: app downloads/rankings) and gap #14 (app-store review scrapers) as a zero-cost, no-login method to build our own point-in-time panel of Airbnb's and competitors' App Store rank and review-count going forward from whenever we start running it; does not backfill history.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only per call; historical series would require our own scheduled captures going forward

candidates.name: google-play-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js scraper (MIT, 2963 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026) for Google Play store pages: install-count buckets (e.g. "100M+"), rating count, rating average, category chart rank (top-free/top-grossing lists), and reviews text, for any Android package id including com.airbnb.android and competitors (com.booking, com.tripadvisor, com.expedia.bookings). No auth needed, no data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Same as the iOS counterpart -- free, no-key method to build a going-forward Android download/rank/review-count time series for Airbnb vs. Booking/Expedia/Vrbo; the most-starred, most actively maintained project in this space, with a whole family of derivative wrappers (see google-play-api, JoMingyu port).
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only; no historical archive

candidates.name: google-play-scraper (Python port)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python port (MIT, 1011 stars, updated 11 Sep 2026) of facundoolano's Node library with an identical field set (install buckets, rating count, category rank). Easier to slot into our existing pandas/duckdb pipeline than the JS original.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as the Node original but directly usable from our Python stack without a Node bridge; worth noting as the drop-in choice if we build a scheduled Android app-metrics puller.

candidates.name: apprankings
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python tool (MIT, 42 stars) purpose-built to poll Apple's public top-charts RSS/JSON feeds for a given category/country and log an app's chart position over time to a local store. Last commit Oct 2023 (stale but the endpoint it hits, Apple's public RSS charts, is still live).
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets 'rank history' rather than a one-off snapshot -- closest match in this search to a true App Store ranking-history tracker; would need reviving/re-pointing at Travel category + Airbnb's app id, and only starts producing history from whenever it is run.
candidates.time_coverage: snapshot-forward from whenever run; unmaintained since 2023

candidates.name: itunes-app-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Simple Python scraper (MIT, 56 stars) from the Digital Methods Initiative (University of Amsterdam academic group behind 4CAT) for iTunes/App Store search and category-chart data, including app rank within charts and metadata.
candidates.why_useful: An academic-group-maintained, citeable alternative to the hobbyist scrapers above for the same iOS rank/metadata pull; DMI tools are often paired with 4CAT for longitudinal capture, so this is the more 'replication package'-flavored option if we want a citable method.

candidates.name: gplay-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python Google Play scraper (MIT, 308 stars, updated 12 Sep 2026) advertised as extracting 65+ fields per app: install counts, rating distribution, review counts, developer info, ASO metrics, category rank.
candidates.why_useful: Wider field coverage than the base google-play-scraper (e.g. rating histogram, not just average) -- useful if the team wants a richer engagement snapshot for Airbnb's Android app and peers in one call.

candidates.name: sensortower-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (no listed license, 1 star, last commit Feb 2025) of the public app.sensortower.com pages to collect download-estimate statistics for Android and iOS apps -- i.e. it reads Sensor Tower's free public app-detail pages rather than calling their paid API.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets our gap #5 wish-list item 'AppFigures/Sensor Tower/data.ai open samples' -- if Sensor Tower's public pages still expose download estimates for Airbnb/Booking/Expedia without a paid key, this is a free route to third-party download-estimate numbers (Sensor Tower's own modeled downloads, not just store rank). Small, unmaintained repo -- would need testing/adapting and a ToS check before any run (per repo rules, scraping decision left to a human).
candidates.geography: global (per Sensor Tower's own country breakdowns)
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only; unmaintained since Feb 2025

candidates.name: app-store-operator
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server (MIT, 3 stars, updated 25 Jul 2026) billed as 'Free App Store competitive intelligence for Claude -- rival downloads, revenue, and ASO keywords... no subscription.' Wraps public App Store data sources to estimate downloads/revenue/keyword rank for any app, framed for use by an LLM agent.
candidates.why_useful: If it genuinely derives download/revenue estimates from free public signals (as advertised) rather than a paid Sensor Tower/data.ai feed, it is a zero-cost way to get modeled download/revenue numbers for Airbnb's app and travel competitors; needs verification of its actual data source before relying on it, and is very small/unverified (3 stars).

candidates.name: appfigures/cli
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Appfigures CLI and MCP server (Apache-2.0, 20 stars, updated 2 Sep 2026) for pulling sales/rank/review data from the Appfigures API for apps you (or a free-tier account) have access to.
candidates.why_useful: Official, maintained client for Appfigures -- the vendor named directly in our gap list -- but almost certainly requires an Appfigures account/API key, and free-tier access is normally limited to apps you own (i.e. would not give third-party Airbnb download data without a paid plan). Worth flagging as the correct tool if the team ever gets/considers an Appfigures trial key, but not usable as-is without one.

candidates.name: sensortowerR
candidates.what_it_holds: R interface (custom/other license, 6 stars, updated 13 May 2026) to the official (paid) Sensor Tower API, covering downloads, revenue, and rank endpoints.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Sensor Tower has an R client, but the underlying API is paid/keyed -- not usable without a Sensor Tower subscription, so low value unless the team already has or can trial API access.

candidates.name: sensortower-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server (no listed license, 17 stars, updated 2 Jul 2026) exposing Sensor Tower's official (paid) API endpoints as tools for an LLM agent.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat as the R client -- convenient wrapper but gated behind a paid Sensor Tower key; only useful if the team obtains one.

candidates.name: app-store-scraper (review scraper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-API App Store review scraper (MIT, 102 stars, updated 16 Jul 2026); pulls per-app review text, rating, and timestamps from Apple's storefront.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at Airbnb's App Store id to build a review-volume-over-time proxy (a cheap stand-in for review-count time series / app-store review scrapers, gap #14), but overlaps heavily with facundoolano/app-store-scraper's review endpoint.
candidates.time_coverage: snapshot of currently-visible reviews only (Apple does not expose full historical review archives)

candidates.name: apple-app-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apple App Store review scraper with a backoff strategy for rate limiting (MIT, 22 stars, updated 27 Apr 2026); also forked as Dinoxel/apple-app-reviews-scraper (8 stars).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal addition to the review-scraper family above; the backoff handling could make a scheduled Airbnb-review-volume pull more reliable, but no new data or method beyond what facundoolano/app-store-scraper offers.

candidates.name: google-play-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Turns google-play-scraper into a RESTful API server (MIT, 389 stars, updated 5 Sep 2026) -- same underlying fields (install buckets, rating, category rank), just exposed over HTTP instead of as a library import.
candidates.why_useful: Convenience wrapper only; no new fields versus the base google-play-scraper. Noted for completeness since it appeared prominently in results, but adds nothing the base library doesn't already give us.

notes: This theme is almost entirely 'method', not 'data' -- neither Apple nor Google exposes a public historical rank/download archive, and no GitHub repo found holds a committed Airbnb (or travel-app) rank/download/review-count time series; every usable repo is a scraper/client that would need to be run on a schedule starting today to build a series, which caps upside for a pitch due 2 Oct. The one exception worth flagging for a human ToS call is lorainemg/sensortower-scraper, which claims to pull Sensor Tower's own download *estimates* (not just store rank) from public pages without a paid key -- if real and still working, this is the closest thing to a free data.ai/Sensor Tower sample in this search, but it is unmaintained (last commit Feb 2025) and unverified. Two of six search calls were partly unproductive: the broad 'app rank history' OR query returned zero results (gh search treats OR loosely / phrase matching is strict), and the 'sensor tower/app annie/data.ai dataset' query surfaced generic ML-dataset repos with no relevance, wasting a call -- a scout repeating this theme should skip that phrasing and instead try `--topic=app-store` / `--topic=aso` or WebSearch for 'data.ai open dataset site:github.com' if more budget is available. Did not attempt gh search code or clone anything, per instructions.
